gen-dafont-groovy-gf-pt-sans-caption: Groovy squeezes its c almost shut, with loose, friendly spacing. PT Sans Caption opens its bowls wide and carries big-bodied lowercase, so paragraphs feel inviting and easy going rather than cramped.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-radio-canada-big: Radio Canada Big lets its monoline letters fill the line, terminals stopping short of each stem. Radio Canada Big sits beneath Groovy, plain and open where the heading is tight and funky.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-readex-pro: Friendly and funky, Groovy pinches its c almost shut and spaces its lowercase loosely. Readex Pro does best with broad terminal gaps and steady weight, the quiet job Groovy never attempts.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-roboto: Tight-lipped letters up top, wide-mouthed ones underneath, and nothing fussy in between. Roboto opens its round letters with generous mouths, while Groovy turns cramped if you make it small.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-saira: Pinched, playful letters up top, and see-through ones waiting just underneath. Saira does best with a visible gap in each s and rounded letters stretching high, while Groovy does best at funk.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-sarpanch: Sarpanch keeps its lowercase e clearly open and its ascenders tucked close to the x-height beneath the Groovy heading. The standout quality is plain outlines up top meeting open letters below.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-savate: Squeezed shapes above, open jaws below, and all of it friendly. Savate rounds its o almost as tall as a capital O, while Groovy holds every arm and leg to constant width.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-schibsted-grotesk: Groovy pinches its c into a narrow slit, with loosely tracked lowercase and uniform strokes. Schibsted Grotesk, with big open e and a, holds up at modest sizes, so give Groovy the larger size.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-sen: Groovy draws every arm and leg at a constant width, with its c nearly sealed into a slit. Sen rises tall, its curves ending open, an easy partner on the page.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-sintony: Groovy pinches its c down to a narrow slit and lets its lowercase run loosely tracked. Sintony, a sans-serif with a chunky tall midzone and no clogged curves, reads smoothly paragraph after paragraph.
